sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Warren County, Ohio?
sections.html:
Warren County deeds go to the recorder at 406 Justice Drive, Lebanon, OH 45036, the same Justice Drive campus that houses the auditor. The office phone is 513-695-1382 or 513-695-1383, and the fax line is 513-695-2949.

Checks are made payable to the Warren County Recorder. The counter wants the precise amount and sends back any short payment without recording it, and it suggests that frequent filers open an escrow account so an over or under payment does not hold up a same-day recording. Typical turnaround on a filing is 24 hours.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Warren County for a home seller?
sections.html:
Warren County sits in southwestern Ohio and is part of the Cincinnati metropolitan area. Lebanon is the seat and Mason is the most populous city. The county was created on May 1, 1803 out of Hamilton County, covers about 407 square miles, and is shaped like a rough square roughly twenty miles on a side.

The 2020 census counted 242,337 residents, with 77.2 percent of occupied homes owner-occupied among 93,276 housing units. The Little Miami River zigzags through the county, the Great Miami touches its northwest corner, and Caesar Creek Lake sits in Massie Township. Ten school districts serve the county: Carlisle, Clinton-Massie, Franklin, Kings, Lebanon, Little Miami, Loveland, Mason, Springboro and Wayne, along with the Warren County Career Center. The county's list of local governments names sixteen municipalities, including Lebanon, Mason, Springboro, Franklin, Monroe, Carlisle, Waynesville and Loveland, along with eleven townships.

County government is concentrated in Lebanon. The second courthouse went up in 1835 at East and Silver Streets and was renovated in 1998 for county offices, while the Justice Center, the jail, the sheriff and the juvenile and probate court sit on Justice Drive. A 100,000 square foot administration building opened there in 2001.

sections.h2: What does the Warren County recorder charge to record?
sections.html:
The recorder's fee page carries a schedule dated October 17, 2019, which tracks the amounts set in Revised Code 317.32.

Selected Warren County recording fees (Warren County Recorder fee schedule)
ItemFee
First two pages$34.00
Each additional page$8.00
Copies made by staff$2.00
Subdivision plat, 24 by 36 inches$86.40 per page
Federal lien$5.00
Federal release$3.00
Zoning resolution$50.00
Zoning amendment$20.00
Financing statement (real estate only)$12.00
Each name indexed on a financing statement$4.00

The recorder's notice says the office does not charge the optional $5 digital preservation fee. If a filer sends the extra $5 anyway, the office keeps it instead of rejecting the paper for incorrect fees. Marginal notations for indexing earlier instruments also carry no charge. Members of the public who copy documents themselves pay 25 cents per page.

sections.h2: How do you search Warren County land records online?
sections.html:
Most documents have been online since April 20, 2016, and the recorder reports that all deeds are indexed and viewable back to 1797. The search runs through a land records page that works best with the parcel number. The 10-digit parcel number appears in the upper left corner of an address or name search on the auditor's property site.

To save a copy, scroll to the bottom of the open document, click the print icon and use the PDF that opens. The recorder's page adds that more than 5 million documents have been recorded in the county, and staff will help by phone at 513-695-1382.

  • E-recording works for every document type except plats.
  • Every land record must include a legal description.
  • A transfer document that needs to be re-recorded must be redone with new notarized signatures, a rule shared by the recorder and the auditor.
  • A free property fraud alert sends an email, text or phone message when a document is filed on a parcel you own. People without a computer can sign up by calling the office.

sections.h2: What does the Warren County auditor require before a deed reaches the recorder?
sections.html:
Ohio makes the auditor transfer the deed first, and the Warren County auditor's transfer page lists what must be in order. Missing any item sends the deed back.

  • A properly completed Statement of Value and Receipt (DTE Form 100), or a Statement of Reason for Exemption (DTE Form 100 EX), plus the fees payable to the Warren County Auditor.
  • A grantor name that matches the way the grantor took title in the prior deed.
  • A reference to the previous deed of record, written on the new deed.
  • Approval and initials from the map department before the deed is presented to the auditor.
  • Form DTE 102 when the parcel is, or last year was, in the CAUV farm program.
  • The grantor's signature, notarized.

The page prints the fees as follows: a mandatory conveyance fee of $1.00 per thousand dollars of the purchase price under 319.54, a county transfer tax of $2.00 per thousand under 322.02, for a combined $3.00 per thousand, with leftover pennies bumped up to the next dime, and a $0.50 transfer fee per parcel. The $2.00 figure is the permissive levy the county commissioners adopted.

sections.h2: Which Warren County transfers are exempt from the conveyance fee?
sections.html:
An exempt transfer uses form 100 EX, where the grantee checks one reason from a lettered list on the back. Reasons (b), (g) and (m) need a notarized affidavit explaining the facts, since the auditor wants to know why no money changed hands.

Under section 319.54 the exempt categories include:

  • Transfers to or from governments and their agencies.
  • Deeds that exist only to secure or release a debt.
  • Confirmation and correction deeds.
  • Gifts between spouses and between parents and children.
  • Sales for delinquent taxes or assessments.
  • Deeds that put property into, or take it out of, a trust the maker can revoke.
  • Transfers among heirs when no consideration is paid.

sections.h2: How must a deed be signed to be accepted in Warren County?
sections.html:
The auditor's page requires the grantor to sign any deed executed in Ohio and have it notarized. That tracks section 5301.01, which lets a judge, a court clerk, a county auditor, a county engineer, a notary or a mayor take the acknowledgment.

The recorder is the final stop. Under section 5301.25 an unrecorded deed is treated as fraudulent against a later good-faith buyer who had no knowledge of it. Getting the deed on the Warren County record promptly after closing closes that gap.

sections.h2: What does the Warren County recorder keep, and what is handled elsewhere?
sections.html:
The recorder answers the questions on its FAQ page plainly: the county uses tract (geographical) indexing, has no registered land (Torrens) system, does not sell blank forms, and records military discharge papers (DD214). A mailed filing has to include return postage or a prepaid envelope.

People often arrive at this office for papers it does not hold. Vital records and court files sit with other departments, and the recorder's page gives these numbers:

  • Birth and death records: 513-695-1220.
  • Marriage licenses: 513-695-1183.
  • Divorce records: 513-695-1120.

sections.h2: Who collects Warren County property tax on a home being sold?
sections.html:
The county treasurer, whose office hours run Monday through Friday from 7:30 am to 4:30 pm. Online payment goes through the county's myWarrenCountyOhio portal, and the pay-by-phone number is 513-496-2931. For tax year 2025 the first half came due February 25, 2026, and the second half August 12, 2026, a date the Tax Commissioner extended because the new inflation cap credit under House Bill 186 delayed the bills.

A seller who has not paid, or whose mortgage servicer pays from escrow, should confirm the balance before closing day so the payoff and the deed fees can be settled together.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Warren County recorder?
faqs.a: Call 513-695-1382 or 513-695-1383, or write to 406 Justice Drive, Lebanon, OH 45036. The recorder's page lists fax at 513-695-2949 and says documents typically turn around in about a day.

faqs.q: What is the Warren County fee to record a deed?
faqs.a: The posted schedule shows $34.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each additional page. The schedule is dated October 17, 2019, and the recorder does not charge the optional $5 preservation fee.
Yes, for every document type except plats. The recorder's page links to the e-recording details, and paper filings still go to the counter at 406 Justice Drive with exact fees.

faqs.q: What happens if my check for Warren County recording is the wrong amount?
faqs.a: The document comes back unrecorded. The recorder requires exact fees and returns shortages without recording, and it recommends an escrow account for filers who want over or under payments handled the same day.

faqs.q: How much is the Warren County transfer fee on a house sale?
faqs.a: The auditor's page prints $1.00 per thousand dollars as the mandatory conveyance fee plus $2.00 per thousand in county transfer tax, a combined $3.00 per thousand, and $0.50 per parcel to transfer it. The grantor pays these to the auditor before recording.
